title: Guns N' Roses
wiki_lead:
Guns N' Roses is an American hard rock band formed in Los Angeles, California, in March 1985 by Axl Rose, Izzy Stradlin, Tracii Guns, and others from L.A. Guns and Hollywood Rose. The classic lineup, Rose (vocals), Slash (lead guitar), Stradlin (rhythm guitar), Duff McKagan (bass), and Steven Adler (drums), was finalized in June 1985. After signing with Geffen Records in 1986, the band released its debut album Appetite for Destruction (1987). Initially slow to sell, it broke through with the "Welcome to the Jungle" music video and went on to sell more than 30 million copies worldwide, becoming the best-selling debut album in the U.S. It produced three Billboard Hot 100 top-ten singles: "Welcome to the Jungle", "Paradise City", and the band's only number-one, "Sweet Child o' Mine". The follow-up, G N' R Lies (1988), reached number two and featured the top-five single "Patience".
Adler was fired in 1990 and replaced by Matt Sorum. The twin albums Use Your Illusion I and II (1991) debuted at numbers two and one on the Billboard 200 and sold a combined 35 million copies worldwide. The Illusion albums featured high-budget music videos, including "November Rain", which reached number three on the Billboard Hot 100 and later became the first 1990s music video to reach one billion YouTube views. The subsequent Use Your Illusion Tour (1991–93) was marked by the Riverport Riot and other incidents; Stradlin left mid-tour and was replaced by Gilby Clarke, who appeared on the punk covers album "The Spaghetti Incident?" (1993). Clarke was later replaced by Paul Tobias, whose presence contributed to friction that led Slash, Sorum and McKagan to leave between 1996 and 1997. By 1998, only Rose and keyboardist Dizzy Reed remained from the Illusion era.
Rose rebuilt the band with a rotating cast that included Brain, Buckethead, Frank Ferrer, Robin Finck, Richard Fortus, Josh Freese, Chris Pitman, Reed, Tommy Stinson, Ron "Bumblefoot" Thal, and Tobias. The long-delayed Chinese Democracy (2008), reportedly the most expensive album ever made at $13 million, debuted at number three but undersold expectations and was banned in China. The Chinese Democracy Tour (2001-2011) included cancelled dates and riots. After years of public feuding, Slash and McKagan rejoined the band in 2016 for the Not in This Lifetime... Tour, which grossed $563.3 million and ranked as the second-highest-grossing concert tour at the time. Since the reunion, the band has released deluxe editions of Appetite for Destruction (2018) and Use Your Illusion (2022), a remastered Live Era '87–'93 (2025), and new singles "Absurd", "Hard Skool" (2021),  "Perhaps" (2023), "Nothin'" and "Atlas" (2025). The current lineup is Rose, Slash, McKagan, rhythm guitarist Fortus, drummer Isaac Carpenter, and keyboardists Reed and Melissa Reese.
Guns N' Roses has sold more than 100 million records worldwide. Greatest Hits (2004) is one of the longest-charting albums in the history of the Billboard 200. Their early sound fused punk, blues, hard rock, and metal; the Illusion albums added progressive and art rock elements, and Chinese Democracy incorporated industrial and electronic textures. Appetite for Destruction is credited with helping end the late-1980s glam metal craze and was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 2024. The band was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2012, though Rose declined to attend. Incidents including Rose's 1987 arrest in Atlanta, the deaths of two fans at the 1988 Monsters of Rock festival, and multiple riots earned the band the label "the most dangerous band in the world". Controversies arose over lyrics (notably "One in a Million"), a hidden Charles Manson cover on "The Spaghetti Incident?", chronic late concert starts and long gaps between albums.

History


Formation (1985–1986)

In 1983, guitarist Tracii Guns introduced Chris Weber to Izzy Stradlin, who soon formed a band with Stradlin's childhood friend, Axl Rose. After several lineup changes, the group became Hollywood Rose. Guitarist Slash replaced Weber in mid-1984, and the group dissolved that August. Rose later joined Guns's band L.A. Guns on Stradlin's recommendation. Rose made his debut with L.A. Guns at the Troubadour on October 5, 1984, on a bill with London, Stradlin's band at the time, and left within weeks. On New Year's Eve 1984, Rose and Stradlin briefly reunited as Hollywood Rose for a one-off show, which included the first live performance of "Don't Cry".
Rose, Stradlin, Guns, Gardner, and bassist Ole Beich formed Guns N' Roses in March 1985. Guns recalled the formation of the band in a 2019 interview, stating: "Axl got into an argument with our manager and our manager fired Axl... So, that same night we started Guns N' Roses... I called Izzy the next day and said, 'Hey, we are gonna start this new band called Guns N' Roses, do you want in?'". The name, which combined those of their previous bands, was devised in late 1984 and was initially intended for a record label. Rejected names included "Heads of Amazon" and "AIDS".
After two rehearsals, Beich, who had stopped responding to the band, was replaced by Duff McKagan, a Seattle musician who lived across the street from Stradlin. Their first rehearsal with McKagan was recorded, and three songs—"Don't Cry", "Think About You" and "Anything Goes"—were aired during their first radio interview, two days before their debut show at the Troubadour on March 26, 1985. Plans for an EP featuring those songs and a cover of "Heartbreak Hotel" were abandoned when Guns and Gardner both left in the spring of 1985. Slash, who had just joined the band Black Sheep, agreed to replace Guns after Rose and Stradlin approached him at a Black Sheep show on May 31, and Steven Adler took over on drums.

The "classic" lineup, Rose, Stradlin, Slash, McKagan, and Adler, was finalized on June 4, 1985. After two rehearsals, they played their first show on June 6 at the Troubadour, on a bill with Mistreater and Fineline. Stradlin and McKagan soon cut down Adler's double-bass drum kit, leaving him with the stripped-down setup that became his trademark. The day after the first show, the band set out on a short West Coast tour booked by McKagan. When the car towing their equipment trailer broke down near Bakersfield, the band hitchhiked roughly a thousand miles north with only their guitars, and played the only date of the tour in Seattle on June 8 using instruments borrowed from the Fastbacks. The rest of the planned dates were cancelled. McKagan later called the "Hell Tour" a defining moment for the group.
Guns N' Roses gained traction on the Hollywood club circuit, performing at venues like The Troubadour and The Roxy, and by early 1986 were selling out shows at both. In March 1986, they signed with Geffen Records, turning down a more lucrative offer from Chrysalis, which had sought to alter their image. The signing followed a tip to Geffen A&R executive Tom Zutaut. Geffen offered full creative control and a $75,000 advance. After signing, their management rented them a house on the former estate of Cecil B. DeMille in Laughlin Park, which the band dubbed "The Hell House". After the band wrecked the house, their management fired them, and Zutaut persuaded his friend Alan Niven, who also managed Great White, to take over later in 1986.

In the summer of 1986, with no producer settled, Geffen and the band planned a limited "bootleg" release on their own Uzi Suicide label to keep them occupied while they wrote and rehearsed and to build an underground following. The result, the EP Live ?!*@ Like a Suicide, was released on December 12, 1986. The EP included covers of Rose Tattoo's "Nice Boys" and Aerosmith's "Mama Kin", along with two originals: "Reckless Life" and "Move to the City". Though marketed as live recordings, the tracks were studio recordings made with Spencer Proffer at Pasha Studios, with crowd noise from recordings by Quiet Riot and Dio added afterward.


Breakthrough and mass popularity (1987–1989)


Appetite for Destruction
Finding a producer for their debut album was difficult. Geffen declined to send the band to London to work with Bill Price, insisting the record be made in Los Angeles. Paul Stanley of Kiss was considered but rejected after proposing changes to Adler's drum setup. Mutt Lange and Tom Werman were also approached, but Geffen declined due to cost. In June 1986, Zutaut brought in Nazareth guitarist Manny Charlton to produce with the band for a few days. Later that year, Spencer Proffer was brought in and recorded several songs as a test. Ultimately, Mike Clink was selected, having previously worked with Triumph. Zutaut had suggested Clink, whose work on UFO's live album Strangers in the Night the band admired. On November 23, 1986, the band recorded "Shadow of Your Love" with Clink at Rumbo Recorders as a test.
After rehearsals, they entered Rumbo, in Canoga Park, in January 1987. The band recorded the basic tracks largely live, with the guitar amplifiers isolated from the drums and bass, in about two weeks, followed by a month of overdubs. Clink booked Take One Recording Studio in Burbank for guitar and vocal overdubs, and sessions continued until late March; Rose said the recording was finished on March 27, 1987. The schedule was erratic, with the band often unreliable about showing up, and Clink later said the hardest part was getting all five members focused at the same time. Drums were finished in six days, but Rose's vocals took significantly longer, as he insisted on recording one line at a time. The recording's cost has been reported as $140,000 by Clink and as about $365,000 by Niven. In the spring, Rose, Slash and Stradlin travelled to New York to oversee the mixing by Steve Thompson and Michael Barbiero, who had earlier been asked to produce the album but declined, and the album was mastered by George Marino.
Appetite for Destruction, Guns N' Roses' debut album, was released on July 21, 1987. The album's original cover art, painted by Robert Williams and depicting a surreal scene of a monster attacking a rapist robot, was deemed too controversial by retailers. Rose had found the 1978 painting, also titled Appetite for Destruction, on a postcard and proposed it as the cover, and the band took the album's title from it. After struggling to reach Williams, Rose and Niven drove to meet him to ask permission. Warner Bros. refused to print the original cover, so the band had to use an outside printer. A feminist group in California called the image a "glorification of rape". The band described the artwork as "a symbolic social statement, with the robot representing the industrial system that's raping and polluting our environment." A revised cover, created by Andy Engell from a design by tattoo artist Bill White Jr., featured skull caricatures of the five band members arranged on a cross, and the original painting was moved to the inner sleeve. The album also carried a parental advisory sticker because of its language, which the band dismissed as pointless.
The band's first single, "It's So Easy", was released exclusively in the UK on June 15, 1987, reaching number 84 on the UK Singles Chart. It was timed to coincide with the band's first performances outside the U.S., three shows at London's Marquee Club on June 19, 22 and 28, a trip manager Alan Niven financed with sales of Live ?!*@ Like a Suicide, which had built a cult following in Britain, partly through Kerrang!. In the United States, "Welcome to the Jungle" served as the lead single in October 1987, accompanied by a music video.
For nearly a year, the album and its singles struggled commercially. Appetite for Destruction debuted at number 182 on the Billboard 200 and sold only about 200,000 copies by the end of 1987. The band also struggled to secure tours: planned dates with Stryper and Y&T fell through, and a European tour with Aerosmith collapsed, with the band's reputation making promoters wary. grok_lead: Guns N' Roses is an American hard rock band formed in Los Angeles, California, in March 1985 from the combination of the bands Hollywood Rose and L.A. Guns. The group initially featured vocalist Axl Rose, lead guitarist Tracii Guns, rhythm guitarist Izzy Stradlin, bassist Ole Beich, and drummer Rob Gardner, but soon reconfigured to include Slash on lead guitar, Duff McKagan on bass, and Steven Adler on drums, forming the lineup that recorded their breakthrough debut album Appetite for Destruction in 1987. Appetite for Destruction achieved enormous commercial success, selling over 30 million copies worldwide and earning 18Ã Platinum certification from the RIAA in the United States for shipments exceeding 18 million units. The album's raw blend of hard rock, blues, and punk elements, drawing influences from acts like the Rolling Stones and Aerosmith, distinguished Guns N' Roses from the prevailing glam metal scene and propelled singles like "Sweet Child o' Mine" to global chart-topping status. Overall, the band has sold more than 86 million albums worldwide, cementing their status as one of the best-selling rock acts ever. Despite their early triumphs, Guns N' Roses endured significant internal strife, including substance abuse and interpersonal conflicts that prompted frequent lineup changes, with Axl Rose remaining the sole original member through much of the 1990s and 2000s. These issues contributed to tour disruptions and delayed releases, such as the 2008 album Chinese Democracy, but the 2016 reunion of Rose with Slash and McKagan revitalized the band, leading to lucrative stadium tours. As of 2025, Guns N' Roses continues active touring with a core lineup of Rose, Slash, McKagan, keyboardist Dizzy Reed, guitarist Richard Fortus, and new drummer Isaac Carpenter, who replaced Frank Ferrer earlier in the year.
